name: Maltese First Division
content:
The list of Maltese football champions begins with the original top tier known as the First Division, which was established in 1909 as the country’s first organized football competition. In its early years, the league featured a small and changing number of teams, with Floriana winning the inaugural title in the 1909–10 season. The competition was briefly interrupted during World War II but otherwise continued consistently, forming the foundation of Maltese football.

During this era, Maltese football was largely dominated by two major clubs, Sliema Wanderers and Floriana, often referred to as the “Old Firm” of Malta. They won the majority of championships before 1940 and continued to be dominant in the post-war period, sharing many titles through the 1950s. Over time, other clubs such as Valletta and Hibernians began to challenge their dominance, bringing more competition into the league.

By the late 1970s, the First Division had evolved into a more structured and competitive league, setting the stage for modernization. In 1980, the system was officially rebranded and reorganized into the Maltese Premier League, marking the end of the First Division era while maintaining continuity in the list of national champions.

name: Maltese Premier League
content:
Since 1980, the top tier of Maltese football has been known as the Maltese Premier League, continuing the same championship lineage as the First Division. The competition is played in a round-robin format, where the team finishing first at the end of the season is crowned national champion. It remains the highest level of football in Malta and includes promotion and relegation with lower divisions.

In the Premier League era, dominance has been shared among several leading clubs, including Sliema Wanderers, Floriana, Valletta, Hibernians, and Ħamrun Spartans. While Sliema Wanderers and Floriana remain the most successful clubs overall with 26 titles each, Valletta has also been a major force, especially in the late 20th and early 21st centuries. More recently, clubs like Birkirkara and Marsaxlokk have also managed to win titles, reflecting a broader competitive balance.

Today, the Maltese Premier League continues to evolve, featuring a modern structure and participation in European competitions. Despite being a smaller league by UEFA standards, it remains central to Maltese football culture, with current champions such as Ħamrun Spartans highlighting the ongoing competitiveness and development of the league.

name: Maltese FA Trophy
content:
The Maltese FA Trophy is the main national knockout football competition in Malta, organized by the Malta Football Association. It was founded in 1933 after the English Football Association donated a trophy inspired by the FA Cup, symbolizing the close sporting ties between England and Malta. The competition is open to clubs from all levels of Maltese and Gozitan football, making it one of the most inclusive tournaments in the country.

The tournament is played on a knockout basis, with teams entering at different stages depending on their league level. Over time, the format has evolved to include clubs from across the entire football pyramid, increasing competitiveness and the chance for lower-tier teams to face top-division sides. The winner of the competition earns qualification for the UEFA Conference League and also competes in the Maltese Super Cup against the league champion.

Historically, the competition has been dominated by major clubs such as Sliema Wanderers, who hold the record for the most titles. The trophy itself has also undergone changes, including the introduction of a redesigned version in 2016 that reflects its historical roots. Despite Malta’s small footballing scale, the FA Trophy remains a prestigious and highly competitive tournament, often producing surprising results and memorable cup runs.
